entities.summary: Georges II d'Amboise (1488–1550) was a French Roman Catholic bishop and cardinal, born in the late 15th century in Western Europe, during the Renaissance period. As bishop of Arras, he played a key role in the Catholic Reformation and was instrumental in the creation of the Jesuit Order. His influence extended to the European continent, shaping the religious and political landscape of the time. Georges II d'Amboise's legacy continues to be felt in the modern Catholic Church, with his contributions to the development of the Jesuit Order remaining a significant aspect of its history. The French monarchy's favoritism towards the Jesuit Order led to increased tensions between Catholics and Protestants in France, a hallmark of the Reformation. Georges II d'Amboise's cardinalate also granted him access to significant wealth and power, which he used to support the Jesuit cause. He was a key figure in the Council of Trent, where he advocated for the reform of the Catholic Church. Georges II d'Amboise's influence was not limited to the Church; he also played a role in the politics of Western Europe, as a prominent advisor to French monarchs. His involvement in the French royal court and his connections to powerful nobles allowed him to shape policy and influence decision-making. Georges II d'Amboise's contributions to the Catholic Reformation and his role in the development of the Jesuit Order make him a significant figure in the history of Western Europe.
